newsitem.title: CHINA: China slams U.S. over congress bill on Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China slams U.S. over congress bill on Hong Kong.

text.p: China on Thursday criticised the United States for meddling in Hong Kong, saying a U.S. House of Representatives bill calling on Beijing to honour its treaty obligations was gross interference in Chinese affairs.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai said no foreign government had the right to involve itself in matters concerning Hong Kong, which returns to Chinese rule on July 1.
The U.S. House of Representatives on Tuesday approved a bill calling on Beijing to honour a treaty with Britain that promises Hong Kong extensive autonomy after its return to China.
"There are some people in the U.S. Congress who know nothing about realities in Hong Kong and have no idea about China's Hong Kong policy," Cui told a news briefing.
"This kind of gross interference in China's internal affairs is wrong," he said. "We are resolutely opposed to this and definitely cannot accept it."
Sino-U.S. relations have long been strained by disputes over issues ranging from trade to human rights to Taiwan, but both sides have made great efforts to boost ties in recent months.
U.S. Vice President Al Gore is expected in Beijing this month, making him the most senior American official to visit China in eight years.
The trip is part of a series to pave the way for an exchange of presidential visits.

The rapprochement has already had to withstand accusations over human rights and alleged Chinese funding of U.S. politicians, and analysts say Hong Kong is likely to be a new Sino-U.S. diplomatic minefield as the handover nears.

The House of Representatives' bill, approved by a 416-1 vote, declared that failure to ensure an elected legislature for Hong Kong would violate a 1984 agreement with Britain and called on China to honour its treaty obligations.
China has vowed to scrap the British colony's current elected legislature and replace it with a Beijing-backed body already waiting in the wings.
China also plans to roll back legislation introduced by Britain to protect human rights, prompting protests from London and pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong.

The U.S. bill called on China to reconsider its repeal of Hong Kong's bill of rights and for it to respect the independence of the territory's chief executive, civil service, judiciary, police and anti-corruption agency.
U.S. lawmakers should concentrate on trying to play a positive role in Hong Kong instead of making ill-informed judgments on the territory, spokesman Cui said.
